<|channel>thought
The user wants to check system memory usage. The 'free -h' command displays total, used, and free memory in a human-readable format.
<channel|>
{"tool": "bash", "args": "free -h"}

Show me the last 50 lines of the system log.

<|channel>thought
The user is asking to tail the syslog. I can use the 'tail' command with the '-n' flag to specify the number of lines.
<channel|>
{"tool": "bash", "args": "tail -n 50 /var/log/syslog"}

What processes are using the most memory?

<|channel>thought
The user wants to see top memory-consuming processes. I can use 'ps' sorted by memory percentage and limit the output with 'head'.
<channel|>
{"tool": "bash", "args": "ps aux --sort=-%mem | head -n 10"}

Check if the nginx service is currently running.

<|channel>thought
The user wants to check the status of a systemd service. The 'systemctl status' command is the standard way to do this.
<channel|>
{"tool": "bash", "args": "systemctl status nginx"}

Find all files on the system larger than 1 Gigabyte.

<|channel>thought
The user is looking for large files. I can use the 'find' command starting from root '/' filtering by type file and size greater than 1G.
<channel|>
{"tool": "bash", "args": "find / -type f -size +1G"}

Compress the /var/www/html folder into a tar.gz archive.

<|channel>thought
The user wants to archive a directory. The 'tar' command with the 'czvf' flags will create a gzip-compressed archive.
<channel|>
{"tool": "bash", "args": "tar -czvf website_backup.tar.gz /var/www/html"}

Make the script 'deploy.sh' executable.

<|channel>thought
The user needs to change file permissions to allow execution. The 'chmod +x' command applies this permission.
<channel|>
{"tool": "bash", "args": "chmod +x deploy.sh"}

Who is currently logged into this machine?

<|channel>thought
The user wants to see active user sessions. The 'w' or 'who' command lists logged-in users and their activities.
<channel|>
{"tool": "bash", "args": "w"}

Check the DNS records for github.com.

<|channel>thought
The user is requesting DNS resolution. The 'dig' or 'nslookup' commands are standard tools for querying DNS records.
<channel|>
{"tool": "bash", "args": "dig github.com"}

See if the local web server is responding on port 80.

<|channel>thought
The user wants to check local HTTP connectivity. A simple 'curl' request fetching headers will verify the server is responding.
<channel|>
{"tool": "bash", "args": "curl -I http://localhost"}
You are a system automation agent. You must reason about the user's request and then output a strict JSON object with 'tool' and 'args' keys.
Count how many files are in the /etc directory.

<|channel>thought
The user wants a file count. I can list the directory contents, one per line, and pipe it to 'wc -l' to count the lines.
<channel|>
{"tool": "bash", "args": "ls -1 /etc | wc -l"}
You are a system automation agent. You must reason about the user's request and then output a strict JSON object with 'tool' and 'args' keys.
What version of Linux is this machine running?

<|channel>thought
The user wants the OS release information. The standard file containing this on modern Linux distributions is /etc/os-release.
<channel|>
{"tool": "bash", "args": "cat /etc/os-release"}

Restart the docker daemon.

<|channel>thought
The user wants to restart a system service. I must use systemctl with the restart command for the docker service.
<channel|>
{"tool": "bash", "args": "systemctl restart docker"}

Show me the routing table for the network.

<|channel>thought
The user wants to see network routing information. The 'ip route' command is the modern standard for this.
<channel|>
{"tool": "bash", "args": "ip route"}

Are there any listening ports currently active?

<|channel>thought
The user wants to see active network sockets. The 'ss' or 'netstat' command with flags for listening TCP/UDP ports will provide this.
<channel|>
{"tool": "bash", "args": "ss -tuln"}

Change the ownership of the web directory to the 'www-data' user.

<|channel>thought
The user needs to modify file ownership recursively. The 'chown' command with the '-R' flag is required here.
<channel|>
{"tool": "bash", "args": "chown -R www-data:www-data /var/www/html"}

Look for any 'ERROR' strings in the docker logs.

<|channel>thought
The user wants to search logs across container output. I can run docker logs and pipe the output to grep, ignoring case.
<channel|>
{"tool": "bash", "args": "grep -i 'ERROR' /var/lib/docker/containers/*/*.log"}

Check the inode usage on the main filesystem.

<|channel>thought
The user wants to see inode capacity, not just storage size. The 'df -i' command provides inode statistics for mounted filesystems.
<channel|>
{"tool": "bash", "args": "df -i"}

Sync the local documents folder to the backup drive.

<|channel>thought
The user wants to synchronize directories. 'rsync' is the best tool for archiving and syncing with its archive and verbose flags.
<channel|>
{"tool": "bash", "args": "rsync -av /home/user/Documents/ /mnt/backup/"}

Check the hardware CPU information for this machine.

<|channel>thought
The user wants details about the physical CPU. I can read the cpuinfo file or use the lscpu utility for a clean summary.

{"tool": "bash", "args": "lscpu"}
